- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–20%.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., 3–5 day highs) — cap forecast overshoots at 2x recent high or 1.5x 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment shifts sharply from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true trend reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >2.5σ above mean, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows >5% deviation from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average unless sentiment overrides.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility — use 14-day volatility as multiplier for forecast adjustment.
